title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-maya-2026-04-10
content:
Goal: track experiment commands, error snippets, hypotheses and minimal repro attempts for the NaN / quality regressions we've been seeing after enabling INT8/FP8 pipelines on redwood-7b variants. Personal scratchpad -- messy, will clean up into an incident postmortem once root cause is nailed down.

Summary of observed symptoms:
- Intermittent NaN tokens in streaming generation (token probabilities become NaN and generation aborts).
- Some runs show sudden collapse of logits (all -inf) at specific step when sequence length crosses ~1024.
- Issue more common with aggressive FP8 quantization profile (per-tensor symmetric scales) and with fused attention kernels enabled.
- Reproducible 100% with my local repro in a container when I force certain calibration profiles.

Environment snapshot:
- Model: redwood-7b-v2 (fp16 baseline).
- Inference runtime: internal serving-runtime branch: feature/quant-int8-fp8 (commit 8a9f3b).
- CUDA: 12.2, cuDNN: 8600, PyTorch 2.2.1 (built with CUDA 12.2), Triton 2.16.0 for fused kernels.
- Hardware: A100-SXM4 80GB in dedicated dev node.
- Env flags used for debug: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1, PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=0 (left from earlier tests).

Commands / scripts tried (most relevant):
1) Baseline (no quant):
   python run_inference.py --model redwood-7b-v2 --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq-len 2048 --prompt "<long prompt>"
   -> stable, no NaNs.

2) FP8 aggressive profile (to reproduce NaN):
   python run_inference.py --model redwood-7b-v2 --quant fp8 --profile aggressive --batch 1 --seq-len 2048 --prompt "<same prompt>"
   -> reproduces NaN after ~120 tokens (deterministic on my repro container).

3) INT8 per-tensor symmetric (current default in pipeline):
   python run_inference.py --model redwood-7b-v2 --quant int8 --per-channel false --batch 1 --seq-len 2048
   -> sometimes NaN, but lower frequency than FP8 aggressive; correlated with logits collapse during attention softmax.

4) INT8 per-channel (recommended):
   python run_inference.py --model redwood-7b-v2 --quant int8 --per-channel true --batch 1 --seq-len 2048
   -> much more stable, no NaN in 10 runs. Suggests per-channel scales mitigate problem in feedforward layers.

5) Disable fused attention kernel (fall back to reference softmax):
   CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python run_inference.py --model redwood-7b-v2 --quant fp8 --kernel fused_attention=false
   -> NaN disappears. Strong signal that fused attention kernel + fp8 interaction is culprit in at least one path.

Error snippets (copied from logs):
- Runtime log when NaN appears:
  2026-04-10 11:24:02.334 ERROR runtime.infer: logits contains NaN at token_idx=119, layer=encoder.attn.softmax, tensor_name=attn_scores
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "runtime/infer.py", line 412, in generate_step
      probs = stable_softmax(scores)
    ValueError: Found NaN in logits (tensor has NaN)

- CUDA kernel warning (when running with debug flags):
  CUDA_WARN: kernel fused_attention returned NaN (thread 256)

- Lower-level dump (from debug dump of activations):
  layer=mlp.fc2, output mean=nan, std=nan, max=nan, min=nan

Immediate hypotheses:
1) FP8 dynamics overflow: FP8 dynamic range insufficient for attention score accumulation after key-query matmul -> fused softmax receives overflowed inputs and produces NaN.
2) Scale calibration mismatch between matmul outputs and subsequent elementwise kernels (per-tensor scales too coarse).
3) Accumulation precision: fused kernels use TF32 or reduced accumulation causing catastrophic cancellation when sequence large (1024+), leading to NaN when combined with fp8 clipping.
4) KV cache indexing bug interacting with quantized KV cache (less likely because disabling fused attention fixes it).
5) Per-channel scaling seems protective; suggests quantization scales not capturing per-output-channel distribution.

What I've tried to validate hypotheses (results):
- Swapped FP8 -> BF16 for matmuls only (keep activations in fp8 after matmul): reduces frequency but not eliminating NaN. Suggests matmul accumulation benefits from BF16.
- Enabled stochastic rounding in quantizer (experimental): no clear difference.
- Re-run with per-channel INT8: stable.
- Re-run with fused_attention disabled: stable.
- Added NaN-guards in kernel (saturate to large negative before softmax if > threshold): prevents crash but outputs are garbage (quality regression).

Repro script (minimal):
- repo: runtime/quant-repros (local branch maya-debug-8421)
- steps:
  1) docker build -t qr:dbg . (Dockerfile with same runtime stack as prod)
  2) docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 -it qr:dbg /bin/bash
  3) python repro/run_fp8_repro.py --model redwood-7b-v2 --seq-len 2048 --quant fp8 --profile aggressive
  4) wait ~2 minutes -> NaN observed at token ~120 consistently

Next diagnostic steps I want to run (priority ordered):
- Add instrumentation counters inside fused_attention to log pre-softmax min/max/scale per-head just before applying softmax (non-blocking; low overhead). Compare between successful+failed runs.
- Add wide-range calibration run for fp8 (collect activation histograms per-tensor and per-channel across a large prompt corpus) and re-generate scales with percentile=99.999 instead of 99.9.
- Hard-fail early if accumulated matmul contains values outside representable FP8 range (so we get deterministic crash at matmul instead of later NaN).
- Test with BF16 accumulation for matmul + FP8 storage (float32 or bf16 accumulator). See if elimination of NaNs is complete.
- Instrument kernel to run specific head(s) in fp16 to see per-head sensitivity.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- If fused kernel is the root cause, do we: (a) revert fused_attention for FP8 profiles until it's fixed; (b) ship fallback to per-channel INT8 by default; or (c) keep fused kernel but add safe-guards / slower accumulation path for long contexts? Need input from perf/infra on cost tradeoffs.
- Should calibration for FP8 be per-customer workload? (Different prompts generate different activation ranges.) Might need autoscaling of percentile per workload.

Notes for incident write-up (if we confirm fused_attention+fp8):
- Timeline of experiments (include commands above + timestamps).
- Repro instructions + exact commit hashes.
- Impact assessment: % of production requests likely affected (estimate via sampling on prod traces for similar prompts / lengths).
- Temporary mitigations: default to per-channel int8 for >X tokens, or disable FP8 aggressive profile for Hosted API until fix.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add detailed per-layer activation histograms for aggressive FP8 profile.
- [ ] Implement logging in fused_attention and re-run 100 repros to get head-level stats.
- [ ] Coordinate with perf team (Samir) on cost impact of falling back to per-channel INT8.
- [ ] Create JIRA-INV-8421 with experiment notes + attach repro container.

Quick breadcrumbs (timestamps):
- 2026-04-10 09:12 Ran initial repro with fp8 aggressive -> NaN at 119 (see repro logs).
- 2026-04-10 10:05 Tried per-channel int8 -> stable. Noted big diff.
- 2026-04-10 10:40 Disabled fused_attention -> stable. Marked as strong signal.
- 2026-04-10 14:22 Tried BF16 accumulators -> reduced frequency.
- 2026-04-11 08:30 Added kernel-level logging patch, collecting traces for 200 runs.

If anyone reading: ping me (Maya Chen) on Slack #eng-quant if you want to reproduce locally -- I can share the docker image and a short script to run. Will follow up with a cleaned incident doc once we confirm root cause.
